151	def known_windows(versions: list[Version], known_at: int) -> list[Token]:
152	    """Reconstruct the valid windows of one attribute as known at ``known_at``.
153	
154	    Every version is known from its ``recorded_at`` onwards, and every truncation
155	    it carries from the ``recorded_at`` of that truncation onwards.  Working from
156	    the newest version the reader can see back to the oldest, a version holds
157	    valid time from its own ``valid_from`` until the earliest of:
158	
159	    * ``valid_from`` of the next version the reader can see, because the value
160	      written later is the one in force from then on;
161	    * the end it carries for that reader, which is its declared ``valid_end`` or,
162	      while the trim that pulled the end back is still unknown, nothing at all;
163	    * the instant a correction already known at ``known_at`` starts writing
164	      there, which is where the chain of visible corrections takes over.
165	
166	    A version whose only displacers are recorded after ``known_at`` keeps an open
167	    ended window, because at that instant nobody had written the bound — that
168	    rule is what keeps a transaction-time view exact.  Tokens come back in
169	    transaction order, oldest first.  Retraction rows always carry an empty
170	    window: they exist to mark the instant an attribute ceased to exist.
171	    """
172	    ordered = sorted(versions, key=lambda item: (item.valid_from, item.version))
173	    tokens: list[Token] = []
174	    takeover: int | None = None
175	    for index in range(len(ordered) - 1, -1, -1):
176	        version = ordered[index]
177	        if version.recorded_at > known_at:
178	            # Not recorded yet for this reader, and it could not have displaced
179	            # anything either: it is invisible to the whole pass.
180	            continue
181	        following = next(
182	            (
183	                ordered[other]
184	                for other in range(index + 1, len(ordered))
185	                if ordered[other].recorded_at <= known_at
186	            ),
187	            None,
188	        )
189	        if version.operation == "retract":
190	            # A retraction never holds valid time of its own; it only closes the
191	            # window in front of it.
192	            end: int | None = version.valid_from
193	        else:
194	            end = version.end_known_at(known_at)
195	            if following is not None:
196	                # A version the reader can see takes over where it begins.
197	                end = following.valid_from if end is None else min(end, following.valid_from)
198	            if takeover is not None:
199	                # A correction already known at ``known_at`` starts writing at
200	                # that instant, which is the end of everything before it.
201	                end = takeover if end is None else min(end, takeover)
202	        tokens.append((version, version.valid_from, end))
203	        takeover = version.valid_from
204	    tokens.sort(key=lambda token: (token[0].recorded_at, token[0].version))
205	    return tokens
206	
207	
208	def complete_windows(versions: list[Version], known_at: int) -> list[Token]:
209	    """The windows as they stand in the ledger, for a history listing.
210	
211	    Every version the reader can see keeps the end the ledger records for it,
212	    with any trim the reader cannot know about yet left out, so this is the
213	    full-knowledge view of the ledger for that transaction instant rather than a
214	    projection: a window a correction pulled back shows the pulled back end once
215	    that correction is knowable, and a value displaced by a backdated
216	    restatement keeps the part of its own window that no later version took over.
217	    """
218	    ordered = sorted(versions, key=lambda item: (item.valid_from, item.version))
219	    tokens: list[Token] = []
220	    for index, version in enumerate(ordered):
221	        if version.recorded_at > known_at:
222	            # Recorded after the reader's instant, so this reader never saw it.
223	            continue
224	        end = version.end_known_at(known_at)
225	        successor = next(
226	            (
227	                ordered[other]
228	                for other in range(index + 1, len(ordered))
229	                if ordered[other].recorded_at <= known_at
230	            ),
231	            None,
232	        )
233	        if successor is not None:
234	            end = successor.valid_from if end is None else min(end, successor.valid_from)
235	        tokens.append((version, version.valid_from, end))
236	    tokens.sort(key=lambda token: (token[0].valid_from, token[0].version))
237	    return tokens
238

240	def project(tokens: list[Token], at: int) -> Token | None:
241	    """Select the value that was in force at business instant ``at``.
242	
243	    Tokens arrive in transaction order, newest first.  A backdated correction can
244	    leave two windows that touch: the value it displaced keeps the window it had,
245	    and the restated value covers the earlier part of it.  The value written last
246	    is the one the ledger believes from the instant it took effect, so the
247	    newest match wins.
248	    """
249	    for token in reversed(tokens):
250	        start, end = token[1], token[2]
251	        if start <= at and (end is None or at < end):
252	            return token
253	    return None

256	def _value_document(entry: tuple[Any, int, str, int, int | None, int] | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
257	    if entry is None:
258	        return None
259	    value, version, operation, start, end, recorded_at = entry
260	    return {
261	        "value": value,
262	        "version": version,
263	        "operation": operation,
264	        "valid_from": iso(start),
265	        "valid_end": None if end is None else iso(end),
266	        "recorded_at": iso(recorded_at),
267	    }

270	def _batch_operation_name(raw: Any) -> str:
271	    """The idempotency-operation label for a batch request.
272	
273	    It is derived from the request body rather than the key, so reusing one
274	    idempotency key on a *different* batch is detected the same way reusing it
275	    on a single-entity write already is.
276	    """
277	    payload = Store.encode(raw)
278	    digest = hashlib.sha256(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
279	    return f"batch:{digest}"

282	class TimeVault:
283	    """Bitemporal entity store: valid time on one axis, transaction time on the other."""
284	
285	    def __init__(self, database: str, clock: Callable[[], Any] | None = None):
286	        self.store = Store(database, clock)
287	
288	    # -- writes -------------------------------------------------------------
289	
290	    def create_entity(self, entity_type: str, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
291	        moment = self.store.now()
292	        entity = Entity.parse(entity_type, raw)
293	        if "valid_from" in raw:
294	            valid_from = instant(raw["valid_from"], "valid_from")
295	            if valid_from > moment:
296	                raise ValidationError("valid_from must not be in the future")
297	        else:
298	            valid_from = moment
299	
300	        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
301	            return self._create_core(
302	                entity.type, entity.id, entity.attributes, valid_from, recorded_at
303	            )
304	
305	        return self._idempotent(key, f"create:{entity.type}/{entity.id}", action, moment)
306	
307	    def apply_correction(
308	        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, raw: Any, key: str | None
309	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
310	        now = self.store.now()
311	        correction = Correction.parse(raw, now)
312	
313	        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
314	            return self._correct_core(entity_type, entity_id, correction, recorded_at)
315	
316	        return self._idempotent(key, f"correct:{entity_type}/{entity_id}", action, now)
317	
318	    def run_batch(self, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
319	        """Atomically apply an ordered list of creates and corrections.
320	
321	        Every item shares one transaction instant, so the whole batch is one
322	        point on the transaction axis: later items see earlier items' effects,
323	        but no outside reader ever sees a partially applied batch.  Any invalid
324	        or conflicting item aborts the transaction and nothing is stored.
325	        """
326	        moment = self.store.now()
327	        operations = parse_batch(raw, moment)
328	        # Entities this very batch will create, so a correction whose creation
329	        # sits later in the array can be told apart from one that names an
330	        # entity nobody will ever create: the first is an ordering conflict,
331	        # the second is simply not found.
332	        created_here = {
333	            (item.entity_type, item.entity_id)
334	            for item in operations
335	            if isinstance(item, BatchCreate)
336	        }
337	
338	        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
339	            results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
340	            seen_creates: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
341	            for index, item in enumerate(operations, start=1):
342	                target = (item.entity_type, item.entity_id)
343	                try:
344	                    if isinstance(item, BatchCreate):
345	                        start = item.valid_from if item.valid_from is not None else recorded_at
346	                        document = self._create_core(
347	                            item.entity_type,
348	                            item.entity_id,
349	                            item.attributes,
350	                            start,
351	                            recorded_at,
352	                        )
353	                        seen_creates.add(target)
354	                        document["operation"] = "create"
355	                    elif isinstance(item, BatchCorrect):
356	                        try:
357	                            document = self._correct_core(
358	                                item.entity_type,
359	                                item.entity_id,
360	                                item.correction,
361	                                recorded_at,
362	                            )
363	                        except NotFoundError:
364	                            if target in created_here and target not in seen_creates:
365	                                raise ConflictError(
366	                                    f"entity {item.entity_type}/{item.entity_id} is "
367	                                    "corrected before it is created"
368	                                )
369	                            raise
370	                        document["operation"] = "correct"
371	                    else:  # pragma: no cover - parse_batch only yields the two kinds
372	                        raise ValidationError("unknown batch operation")
373	                except TimeVaultError as error:
374	                    message = str(error)
375	                    if not message.startswith("operation "):
376	                        raise type(error)(f"operation {index}: {message}") from error
377	                    raise
378	                results.append(document)
379	            return {"recorded_at": iso(recorded_at), "results": results}
380	
381	        return self._idempotent(key, _batch_operation_name(raw), action, moment)

385	    def entity_as_of(

387	        entity_type: str,
388	        entity_id: str,

390	        known_at: Any = None,
391	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
392	        """Project the entity onto a business instant and a knowledge instant.

394	        Both axes default to the current instant, so a plain GET returns the
395	        entity as it is believed to be right now.  Each argument accepts an RFC
396	        3339 string or an integer count of epoch milliseconds.
397	        """
398	        moment = self.store.now()

400	            entity_type,

402	            moment if as_of is None else instant(as_of, "as_of"),

406	    def history(
407	        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, known_at: Any = None
408	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
409	        row = self.store.entity_row(entity_type, entity_id)
410	        if row is None:
411	            raise NotFoundError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} does not exist")
412	        if known_at is None:
413	            known_at = self.store.now()
414	        else:
415	            known_at = instant(known_at, "known_at")
416	        grouped = self._grouped_versions(entity_type, entity_id)
417	        attributes = []
418	        for name in sorted(grouped):
419	            tokens = complete_windows(grouped[name], known_at)
420	            attributes.append(
421	                {
422	                    "attribute": name,
423	                    "versions": [
424	                        version.as_dict(valid_end) for version, _, valid_end in tokens
425	                    ],
426	                }
427	            )
428	        return {
429	            "type": entity_type,
430	            "id": entity_id,
431	            "created_at": iso(int(row["created_at"])),
432	            "known_at": iso(known_at),
433	            "attributes": attributes,
434	        }

436	    def diff(
437	        self,
438	        entity_type: str,
439	        entity_id: str,
440	        start: Any,
441	        end: Any,
442	        known_at: Any = None,
443	        names: list[str] | None = None,
444	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
445	        start = instant(start, "from")
446	        end = instant(end, "to")
447	        known_at = self.store.now() if known_at is None else instant(known_at, "known_at")
448	        if end <= start:
449	            raise ValidationError("to must be strictly later than from")
450	        if names is not None and len(set(names)) != len(names):
451	            raise ValidationError("attribute may not be repeated")
452	        left = self._projection(entity_type, entity_id, start, known_at)
453	        right = self._projection(entity_type, entity_id, end, known_at)
454	        selected = sorted(set(left) | set(right))
455	        if names is not None:
456	            wanted = set(names)
457	            unknown = sorted(wanted - set(self._all_attributes(entity_type, entity_id)))
458	            if unknown:
459	                raise ValidationError(f"unknown attribute(s): {', '.join(unknown)}")
460	            selected = [name for name in selected if name in wanted]
461	
462	        changes = []
463	        for name in selected:
464	            before = left.get(name)
465	            after = right.get(name)
466	            if before is None and after is None:
467	                continue
468	            if before is not None and after is not None and value_same(before[0], after[0]):
469	                # The value carried across the boundary; only the version that
470	                # supplies it changed, which is not a business-time difference.
471	                continue
472	            if before is None:
473	                kind = "added"
474	            elif after is None:
475	                kind = "removed"
476	            else:
477	                kind = "changed"
478	            changes.append(
479	                {
480	                    "attribute": name,
481	                    "change": kind,
482	                    "before": _value_document(before),
483	                    "after": _value_document(after),
484	                }
485	            )
486	        return {
487	            "type": entity_type,
488	            "id": entity_id,
489	            "from": iso(start),
490	            "to": iso(end),
491	            "known_at": iso(known_at),
492	            "changes": changes,
493	        }

497	    def _create_core(
498	        self,
499	        entity_type: str,
500	        entity_id: str,
501	        attributes: tuple[Any, ...],
502	        valid_from: int,
503	        recorded_at: int,
504	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
505	        """Insert one entity and its version-1 assertions at a fixed instant."""
506	        if self.store.entity_row(entity_type, entity_id) is not None:
507	            raise ConflictError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} already exists")
508	        self.store.insert_entity(entity_type, entity_id, recorded_at)
509	        for attribute in attributes:
510	            self.store.insert_version(
511	                entity_type,
512	                entity_id,
513	                attribute.name,
514	                1,
515	                "assert",
516	                attribute.value,
517	                valid_from,
518	                None,
519	                recorded_at,
520	            )
521	        document = self._read(entity_type, entity_id, recorded_at, recorded_at)
522	        document["created_at"] = iso(recorded_at)
523	        return document

525	    def _correct_core(
526	        self,
527	        entity_type: str,
528	        entity_id: str,
529	        correction: Correction,
530	        recorded_at: int,
531	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
532	        """Apply one already-parsed correction at a fixed transaction instant.
533	
534	        Raises :class:`NotFoundError` when the entity does not exist yet and
535	        :class:`ConflictError` when the correction's facts would land before the
536	        entity was recorded.
537	        """
538	        row = self.store.entity_row(entity_type, entity_id)
539	        if row is None:
540	            raise NotFoundError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} does not exist")
541	        if int(row["created_at"]) > recorded_at:
542	            raise ConflictError(
543	                f"cannot state a fact about {entity_type}/{entity_id} before it existed"
544	            )
545	        for fact in correction.facts:
546	            self._apply_fact(entity_type, entity_id, fact, recorded_at)
547	        # ``as_of`` equal to the instant just recorded means "every window
548	        # that starts when this fact takes effect", which describes the
549	        # attribute as it stands after the correction rather than the state
550	        # that the correction replaced.  A write is never a 404, so an
551	        # entity with nothing in effect right now answers with no attributes.
552	        return self._read(entity_type, entity_id, recorded_at, recorded_at, required=False)
553	
554	    def _idempotent(
555	        self,
556	        key: str | None,
557	        operation: str,
558	        action: Callable[[int], dict[str, Any]],
559	        moment: int,
560	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
561	        """Run ``action`` once per ``key`` and remember the first response.
562	
563	        The whole check-and-write happens in one immediate transaction so two
564	        concurrent deliveries of the same key cannot both run the action.
565	        """
566	        if not key:
567	            raise ValidationError("Idempotency-Key header is required")
568	        with self.store.transaction() as connection:
569	            remembered = self.store.remembered_operation(key)
570	            if remembered is not None:
571	                if remembered != operation:
572	                    raise ConflictError(
573	                        "idempotency key was already used for another operation"
574	                    )
575	                row = connection.execute(
576	                    "SELECT response FROM idempotency WHERE key = ?", (key,)
577	                ).fetchone()
578	                return Store.decode(row["response"])
579	            response = action(moment)
580	            self.store.remember(key, operation, response)
581	            return response

583	    def _apply_fact(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, fact: Fact, recorded_at: int) -> None:
584	        """Place one fact on the ledger.
585	
586	        The fact lands at ``fact.valid_from``.  It takes effect in the ledger at
587	        that same instant, or at ``recorded_at`` when the fact is backdated: a
588	        backdated correction is placed in the past but only displaces the tail
589	        it supersedes, it does not restate the time between its own effective
590	        instant and the correction's effective instant.
591	        """
592	        effective = max(fact.valid_from or recorded_at, recorded_at)
593	        # A retraction needs no truncation pass: its own row sits after every
594	        # version recorded before it and bounds the window in front of it.
595	        if not fact.deleted:
596	            self.store.truncate_attribute(
597	                entity_type, entity_id, fact.attribute, fact.valid_from, effective, recorded_at
598	            )
599	        self.store.insert_version(
600	            entity_type,
601	            entity_id,
602	            fact.attribute,
603	            self.store.next_version(entity_type, entity_id, fact.attribute),
604	            fact.operation,
605	            fact.value,
606	            fact.valid_from,
607	            # A retraction is stored as an empty window at the instant the
608	            # attribute ceased to exist.  It is never selectable by as_of; it
609	            # exists so the window before it has a boundary and so the history
610	            # records that the attribute was withdrawn rather than corrected.
611	            fact.valid_from if fact.deleted else fact.valid_end,
612	            recorded_at,
613	        )
614	
615	    def _grouped_versions(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str) -> dict[str, list[Version]]:
616	        """Every version of the entity, with the trims it took attached.
617	
618	        A trim lives in its own append-only row, so one version can carry several
619	        — one per correction that closed its window.  They are loaded once here
620	        and attached by version number, which is what lets a projection drop the
621	        trims the reader cannot know about yet.
622	        """
623	        events: dict[str, dict[int, list[Truncation]]] = {}
624	        for row in self.store.truncations_for_entity(entity_type, entity_id):
625	            version = int(row["version"])
626	            by_version = events.setdefault(str(row["attribute"]), {})
627	            by_version.setdefault(version, []).append(
628	                Truncation(
629	                    version=version,
630	                    recorded_at=int(row["recorded_at"]),
631	                    valid_end=int(row["valid_end"]),
632	                )
633	            )
634	        grouped: dict[str, list[Version]] = {}
635	        for row in self.store.versions_for_entity(entity_type, entity_id):
636	            version = Version.from_row(row)
637	            attached = events.get(version.attribute, {}).get(version.version, [])
638	            grouped.setdefault(version.attribute, []).append(
639	                version.with_truncations(tuple(attached))

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Callable

from .errors import ConflictError, NotFoundError, TimeVaultError, ValidationError
from .model import (
    BatchCorrect,
    BatchCreate,
    Correction,
    Entity,
    Fact,
    INFINITY,
    instant,
    iso,
    parse_batch,
    value_same,
)
from .store import Store


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Truncation:
    """One window-closing event, stamped on both axes.

    ``recorded_at`` is the transaction instant the system learned the new bound,
    ``valid_end`` the business instant the window was closed at.
    """

    version: int
    recorded_at: int
    valid_end: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Version:
    """One stored attribute version, as read back from the database.

    ``valid_from`` is the business instant the value starts at.  ``declared_end``
    is the bound the assertion itself declared and never moves; ``valid_end`` is
    where the window ends once every correction so far has been applied, so it is
    ``None`` while the window is open ended.  ``recorded_at`` is the transaction
    instant the row was written.
    """

    attribute: str
    version: int
    operation: str
    value: Any
    valid_from: int
    valid_end: int | None
    declared_end: int | None
    recorded_at: int
    truncations: tuple[Truncation, ...] = ()

    @classmethod
    def from_row(cls, row: Any) -> "Version":
        return cls(
            attribute=str(row["attribute"]),
            version=int(row["version"]),
            operation=str(row["operation"]),
            value=None if row["value"] is None else Store.decode(row["value"]),
            valid_from=int(row["valid_from"]),
            valid_end=None if row["valid_end"] is None else int(row["valid_end"]),
            declared_end=None if row["declared_end"] is None else int(row["declared_end"]),
            recorded_at=int(row["recorded_at"]),
        )

    def with_truncations(self, events: tuple[Truncation, ...]) -> "Version":
        return Version(
            self.attribute,
            self.version,
            self.operation,
            self.value,
            self.valid_from,
            self.valid_end,
            self.declared_end,
            self.recorded_at,
            events,
        )

    def known_truncations(self, known_at: int) -> tuple[Truncation, ...]:
        return tuple(event for event in self.truncations if event.recorded_at <= known_at)

    def superseded_at(self) -> int | None:
        """The transaction instant this version stopped being current, if it has.

        That is the instant of a trim, never a business instant, so together with
        ``recorded_at`` it bounds a half-open transaction interval and can never
        precede it.  When several corrections closed the same window the last one
        is the authoritative closure, because it is the one the ledger's final
        ``valid_end`` comes from; the earlier trims stay in the row's truncation
        events, which is how a reader before a later trim still sees the end that
        trim had not yet moved.
        """
        return None if not self.truncations else self.truncations[-1].recorded_at

    def end_known_at(self, known_at: int) -> int | None:
        """Where this version's window ended as of ``known_at``.

        The window end is never later than the bound the assertion declared, so
        the answer is the earliest of that declared bound and every trim the
        reader already knows about.  A trim recorded after ``known_at`` is not
        knowledge yet, so the window it closed is still open ended — that is what
        keeps the upper axis exact.
        """
        end = self.declared_end
        for event in self.known_truncations(known_at):
            end = event.valid_end if end is None else min(end, event.valid_end)
        if end is None:
            return None
        # ``valid_end`` already folds in every trim, including ones this reader
        # has not learned yet, so it is only ever a safe ceiling for the end the
        # reader knows — never a later bound leaking backwards.
        return self.valid_end if self.valid_end is None else min(end, self.valid_end)

    def as_dict(self, valid_end: Any = ...) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Render the version, optionally with a recomputed window end.

        Pass ``None`` explicitly to report an open ended window; omitting the
        argument reports the end as it stands in the ledger for the reader.
        """
        end = self.valid_end if valid_end is ... else valid_end
        declared = self.declared_end
        if declared is None or end is None or end >= declared:
            declared_field: str | None = None
        else:
            declared_field = iso(declared)
        return {
            "attribute": self.attribute,
            "version": self.version,
            "operation": self.operation,
            "value": self.value,
            "valid_from": iso(self.valid_from),
            "valid_from_ms": self.valid_from,
            "valid_end": None if end is None else iso(end),
            "valid_end_ms": end,
            "declared_end": declared_field,
            "recorded_at": iso(self.recorded_at),
            "superseded_at": None
            if self.superseded_at() is None
            else iso(self.superseded_at()),
        }


Token = tuple[Version, int, int | None]
Projection = dict[str, tuple[Any, int, str, int, int | None, int]]


def known_windows(versions: list[Version], known_at: int) -> list[Token]:
    """Reconstruct the valid windows of one attribute as known at ``known_at``.

    Every version is known from its ``recorded_at`` onwards, and every truncation
    it carries from the ``recorded_at`` of that truncation onwards.  Working from
    the newest version the reader can see back to the oldest, a version holds
    valid time from its own ``valid_from`` until the earliest of:

    * ``valid_from`` of the next version the reader can see, because the value
      written later is the one in force from then on;
    * the end it carries for that reader, which is its declared ``valid_end`` or,
      while the trim that pulled the end back is still unknown, nothing at all;
    * the instant a correction already known at ``known_at`` starts writing
      there, which is where the chain of visible corrections takes over.

    A version whose only displacers are recorded after ``known_at`` keeps an open
    ended window, because at that instant nobody had written the bound — that
    rule is what keeps a transaction-time view exact.  Tokens come back in
    transaction order, oldest first.  Retraction rows always carry an empty
    window: they exist to mark the instant an attribute ceased to exist.
    """
    ordered = sorted(versions, key=lambda item: (item.valid_from, item.version))
    tokens: list[Token] = []
    takeover: int | None = None
    for index in range(len(ordered) - 1, -1, -1):
        version = ordered[index]
        if version.recorded_at > known_at:
            # Not recorded yet for this reader, and it could not have displaced
            # anything either: it is invisible to the whole pass.
            continue
        following = next(
            (
                ordered[other]
                for other in range(index + 1, len(ordered))
                if ordered[other].recorded_at <= known_at
            ),
            None,
        )
        if version.operation == "retract":
            # A retraction never holds valid time of its own; it only closes the
            # window in front of it.
            end: int | None = version.valid_from
        else:
            end = version.end_known_at(known_at)
            if following is not None:
                # A version the reader can see takes over where it begins.
                end = following.valid_from if end is None else min(end, following.valid_from)
            if takeover is not None:
                # A correction already known at ``known_at`` starts writing at
                # that instant, which is the end of everything before it.
                end = takeover if end is None else min(end, takeover)
        tokens.append((version, version.valid_from, end))
        takeover = version.valid_from
    tokens.sort(key=lambda token: (token[0].recorded_at, token[0].version))
    return tokens


def complete_windows(versions: list[Version], known_at: int) -> list[Token]:
    """The windows as they stand in the ledger, for a history listing.

    Every version the reader can see keeps the end the ledger records for it,
    with any trim the reader cannot know about yet left out, so this is the
    full-knowledge view of the ledger for that transaction instant rather than a
    projection: a window a correction pulled back shows the pulled back end once
    that correction is knowable, and a value displaced by a backdated
    restatement keeps the part of its own window that no later version took over.
    """
    ordered = sorted(versions, key=lambda item: (item.valid_from, item.version))
    tokens: list[Token] = []
    for index, version in enumerate(ordered):
        if version.recorded_at > known_at:
            # Recorded after the reader's instant, so this reader never saw it.
            continue
        end = version.end_known_at(known_at)
        successor = next(
            (
                ordered[other]
                for other in range(index + 1, len(ordered))
                if ordered[other].recorded_at <= known_at
            ),
            None,
        )
        if successor is not None:
            end = successor.valid_from if end is None else min(end, successor.valid_from)
        tokens.append((version, version.valid_from, end))
    tokens.sort(key=lambda token: (token[0].valid_from, token[0].version))
    return tokens


def project(tokens: list[Token], at: int) -> Token | None:
    """Select the value that was in force at business instant ``at``.

    Tokens arrive in transaction order, newest first.  A backdated correction can
    leave two windows that touch: the value it displaced keeps the window it had,
    and the restated value covers the earlier part of it.  The value written last
    is the one the ledger believes from the instant it took effect, so the
    newest match wins.
    """
    for token in reversed(tokens):
        start, end = token[1], token[2]
        if start <= at and (end is None or at < end):
            return token
    return None


def _value_document(entry: tuple[Any, int, str, int, int | None, int] | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    if entry is None:
        return None
    value, version, operation, start, end, recorded_at = entry
    return {
        "value": value,
        "version": version,
        "operation": operation,
        "valid_from": iso(start),
        "valid_end": None if end is None else iso(end),
        "recorded_at": iso(recorded_at),
    }


def _batch_operation_name(raw: Any) -> str:
    """The idempotency-operation label for a batch request.

    It is derived from the request body rather than the key, so reusing one
    idempotency key on a *different* batch is detected the same way reusing it
    on a single-entity write already is.
    """
    payload = Store.encode(raw)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    return f"batch:{digest}"


class TimeVault:
    """Bitemporal entity store: valid time on one axis, transaction time on the other."""

    def __init__(self, database: str, clock: Callable[[], Any] | None = None):
        self.store = Store(database, clock)

    # -- writes -------------------------------------------------------------

    def create_entity(self, entity_type: str, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        moment = self.store.now()
        entity = Entity.parse(entity_type, raw)
        if "valid_from" in raw:
            valid_from = instant(raw["valid_from"], "valid_from")
            if valid_from > moment:
                raise ValidationError("valid_from must not be in the future")
        else:
            valid_from = moment

        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
            return self._create_core(
                entity.type, entity.id, entity.attributes, valid_from, recorded_at
            )

        return self._idempotent(key, f"create:{entity.type}/{entity.id}", action, moment)

    def apply_correction(
        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, raw: Any, key: str | None
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        now = self.store.now()
        correction = Correction.parse(raw, now)

        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
            return self._correct_core(entity_type, entity_id, correction, recorded_at)

        return self._idempotent(key, f"correct:{entity_type}/{entity_id}", action, now)

    def run_batch(self, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Atomically apply an ordered list of creates and corrections.

        Every item shares one transaction instant, so the whole batch is one
        point on the transaction axis: later items see earlier items' effects,
        but no outside reader ever sees a partially applied batch.  Any invalid
        or conflicting item aborts the transaction and nothing is stored.
        """
        moment = self.store.now()
        operations = parse_batch(raw, moment)
        # Entities this very batch will create, so a correction whose creation
        # sits later in the array can be told apart from one that names an
        # entity nobody will ever create: the first is an ordering conflict,
        # the second is simply not found.
        created_here = {
            (item.entity_type, item.entity_id)
            for item in operations
            if isinstance(item, BatchCreate)
        }

        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
            results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
            seen_creates: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
            for index, item in enumerate(operations, start=1):
                target = (item.entity_type, item.entity_id)
                try:
                    if isinstance(item, BatchCreate):
                        start = item.valid_from if item.valid_from is not None else recorded_at
                        document = self._create_core(
                            item.entity_type,
                            item.entity_id,
                            item.attributes,
                            start,
                            recorded_at,
                        )
                        seen_creates.add(target)
                        document["operation"] = "create"
                    elif isinstance(item, BatchCorrect):
                        try:
                            document = self._correct_core(
                                item.entity_type,
                                item.entity_id,
                                item.correction,
                                recorded_at,
                            )
                        except NotFoundError:
                            if target in created_here and target not in seen_creates:
                                raise ConflictError(
                                    f"entity {item.entity_type}/{item.entity_id} is "
                                    "corrected before it is created"
                                )
                            raise
                        document["operation"] = "correct"
                    else:  # pragma: no cover - parse_batch only yields the two kinds
                        raise ValidationError("unknown batch operation")
                except TimeVaultError as error:
                    message = str(error)
                    if not message.startswith("operation "):
                        raise type(error)(f"operation {index}: {message}") from error
                    raise
                results.append(document)
            return {"recorded_at": iso(recorded_at), "results": results}

        return self._idempotent(key, _batch_operation_name(raw), action, moment)

    # -- reads --------------------------------------------------------------

    def entity_as_of(
        self,
        entity_type: str,
        entity_id: str,
        as_of: Any = None,
        known_at: Any = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Project the entity onto a business instant and a knowledge instant.

        Both axes default to the current instant, so a plain GET returns the
        entity as it is believed to be right now.  Each argument accepts an RFC
        3339 string or an integer count of epoch milliseconds.
        """
        moment = self.store.now()
        return self._read(
            entity_type,
            entity_id,
            moment if as_of is None else instant(as_of, "as_of"),
            moment if known_at is None else instant(known_at, "known_at"),
        )

    def history(
        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, known_at: Any = None
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        row = self.store.entity_row(entity_type, entity_id)
        if row is None:
            raise NotFoundError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} does not exist")
        if known_at is None:
            known_at = self.store.now()
        else:
            known_at = instant(known_at, "known_at")
        grouped = self._grouped_versions(entity_type, entity_id)
        attributes = []
        for name in sorted(grouped):
            tokens = complete_windows(grouped[name], known_at)
            attributes.append(
                {
                    "attribute": name,
                    "versions": [
                        version.as_dict(valid_end) for version, _, valid_end in tokens
                    ],
                }
            )
        return {
            "type": entity_type,
            "id": entity_id,
            "created_at": iso(int(row["created_at"])),
            "known_at": iso(known_at),
            "attributes": attributes,
        }

    def diff(
        self,
        entity_type: str,
        entity_id: str,
        start: Any,
        end: Any,
        known_at: Any = None,
        names: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        start = instant(start, "from")
        end = instant(end, "to")
        known_at = self.store.now() if known_at is None else instant(known_at, "known_at")
        if end <= start:
            raise ValidationError("to must be strictly later than from")
        if names is not None and len(set(names)) != len(names):
            raise ValidationError("attribute may not be repeated")
        left = self._projection(entity_type, entity_id, start, known_at)
        right = self._projection(entity_type, entity_id, end, known_at)
        selected = sorted(set(left) | set(right))
        if names is not None:
            wanted = set(names)
            unknown = sorted(wanted - set(self._all_attributes(entity_type, entity_id)))
            if unknown:
                raise ValidationError(f"unknown attribute(s): {', '.join(unknown)}")
            selected = [name for name in selected if name in wanted]

        changes = []
        for name in selected:
            before = left.get(name)
            after = right.get(name)
            if before is None and after is None:
                continue
            if before is not None and after is not None and value_same(before[0], after[0]):
                # The value carried across the boundary; only the version that
                # supplies it changed, which is not a business-time difference.
                continue
            if before is None:
                kind = "added"
            elif after is None:
                kind = "removed"
            else:
                kind = "changed"
            changes.append(
                {
                    "attribute": name,
                    "change": kind,
                    "before": _value_document(before),
                    "after": _value_document(after),
                }
            )
        return {
            "type": entity_type,
            "id": entity_id,
            "from": iso(start),
            "to": iso(end),
            "known_at": iso(known_at),
            "changes": changes,
        }

    # -- internals ----------------------------------------------------------

    def _create_core(
        self,
        entity_type: str,
        entity_id: str,
        attributes: tuple[Any, ...],
        valid_from: int,
        recorded_at: int,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Insert one entity and its version-1 assertions at a fixed instant."""
        if self.store.entity_row(entity_type, entity_id) is not None:
            raise ConflictError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} already exists")
        self.store.insert_entity(entity_type, entity_id, recorded_at)
        for attribute in attributes:
            self.store.insert_version(
                entity_type,
                entity_id,
                attribute.name,
                1,
                "assert",
                attribute.value,
                valid_from,
                None,
                recorded_at,
            )
        document = self._read(entity_type, entity_id, recorded_at, recorded_at)
        document["created_at"] = iso(recorded_at)
        return document

    def _correct_core(
        self,
        entity_type: str,
        entity_id: str,
        correction: Correction,
        recorded_at: int,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Apply one already-parsed correction at a fixed transaction instant.

        Raises :class:`NotFoundError` when the entity does not exist yet and
        :class:`ConflictError` when the correction's facts would land before the
        entity was recorded.
        """
        row = self.store.entity_row(entity_type, entity_id)
        if row is None:
            raise NotFoundError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} does not exist")
        if int(row["created_at"]) > recorded_at:
            raise ConflictError(
                f"cannot state a fact about {entity_type}/{entity_id} before it existed"
            )
        for fact in correction.facts:
            self._apply_fact(entity_type, entity_id, fact, recorded_at)
        # ``as_of`` equal to the instant just recorded means "every window
        # that starts when this fact takes effect", which describes the
        # attribute as it stands after the correction rather than the state
        # that the correction replaced.  A write is never a 404, so an
        # entity with nothing in effect right now answers with no attributes.
        return self._read(entity_type, entity_id, recorded_at, recorded_at, required=False)

    def _idempotent(
        self,
        key: str | None,
        operation: str,
        action: Callable[[int], dict[str, Any]],
        moment: int,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Run ``action`` once per ``key`` and remember the first response.

        The whole check-and-write happens in one immediate transaction so two
        concurrent deliveries of the same key cannot both run the action.
        """
        if not key:
            raise ValidationError("Idempotency-Key header is required")
        with self.store.transaction() as connection:
            remembered = self.store.remembered_operation(key)
            if remembered is not None:
                if remembered != operation:
                    raise ConflictError(
                        "idempotency key was already used for another operation"
                    )
                row = connection.execute(
                    "SELECT response FROM idempotency WHERE key = ?", (key,)
                ).fetchone()
                return Store.decode(row["response"])
            response = action(moment)
            self.store.remember(key, operation, response)
            return response

    def _apply_fact(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, fact: Fact, recorded_at: int) -> None:
        """Place one fact on the ledger.

        The fact lands at ``fact.valid_from``.  It takes effect in the ledger at
        that same instant, or at ``recorded_at`` when the fact is backdated: a
        backdated correction is placed in the past but only displaces the tail
        it supersedes, it does not restate the time between its own effective
        instant and the correction's effective instant.
        """
        effective = max(fact.valid_from or recorded_at, recorded_at)
        # A retraction needs no truncation pass: its own row sits after every
        # version recorded before it and bounds the window in front of it.
        if not fact.deleted:
            self.store.truncate_attribute(
                entity_type, entity_id, fact.attribute, fact.valid_from, effective, recorded_at
            )
        self.store.insert_version(
            entity_type,
            entity_id,
            fact.attribute,
            self.store.next_version(entity_type, entity_id, fact.attribute),
            fact.operation,
            fact.value,
            fact.valid_from,
            # A retraction is stored as an empty window at the instant the
            # attribute ceased to exist.  It is never selectable by as_of; it
            # exists so the window before it has a boundary and so the history
            # records that the attribute was withdrawn rather than corrected.
            fact.valid_from if fact.deleted else fact.valid_end,
            recorded_at,
        )

    def _grouped_versions(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str) -> dict[str, list[Version]]:
        """Every version of the entity, with the trims it took attached.

        A trim lives in its own append-only row, so one version can carry several
        — one per correction that closed its window.  They are loaded once here
        and attached by version number, which is what lets a projection drop the
        trims the reader cannot know about yet.
        """
        events: dict[str, dict[int, list[Truncation]]] = {}
        for row in self.store.truncations_for_entity(entity_type, entity_id):
            version = int(row["version"])
            by_version = events.setdefault(str(row["attribute"]), {})
            by_version.setdefault(version, []).append(
                Truncation(
                    version=version,
                    recorded_at=int(row["recorded_at"]),
                    valid_end=int(row["valid_end"]),
                )
            )
        grouped: dict[str, list[Version]] = {}
        for row in self.store.versions_for_entity(entity_type, entity_id):
            version = Version.from_row(row)
            attached = events.get(version.attribute, {}).get(version.version, [])
            grouped.setdefault(version.attribute, []).append(
                version.with_truncations(tuple(attached))
            )
        return grouped

    def _all_attributes(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str) -> set[str]:
        return set(self._grouped_versions(entity_type, entity_id))

    def _read(
        self,
        entity_type: str,
        entity_id: str,
        as_of: int,
        known_at: int,
        required: bool = True,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        projection = self._projection(entity_type, entity_id, as_of, known_at, required)
        attributes = {
            name: {
                "value": entry[0],
                "version": entry[1],
                "operation": entry[2],
                "valid_from": iso(entry[3]),
                "valid_end": None if entry[4] is None else iso(entry[4]),
                "recorded_at": iso(entry[5]),
            }
            for name, entry in sorted(projection.items())
        }
        return {
            "type": entity_type,
            "id": entity_id,
            "as_of": iso(as_of),
            "known_at": iso(known_at),
            "attributes": attributes,
        }

    def _projection(
        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, as_of: int, known_at: int, required: bool = True
    ) -> Projection:
        row = self.store.entity_row(entity_type, entity_id)
        if row is None:
            raise NotFoundError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} does not exist")
        if int(row["created_at"]) > known_at:
            raise NotFoundError(
                f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} was not recorded yet at that transaction time"
            )
        grouped = self._grouped_versions(entity_type, entity_id)
        result: Projection = {}
        for name in sorted(grouped):
            window = project(known_windows(grouped[name], known_at), as_of)
            if window is None:
                continue
            version, start, end = window
            result[name] = (
                version.value,
                version.version,
                version.operation,
                start,
                end,
                version.recorded_at,
            )
        if not result and required:
            raise NotFoundError(
                f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} was not in effect at that business instant"
            )
        return result

14	def one(query: dict[str, list[str]], name: str) -> str | None:

36	def make_handler(service: TimeVault) -> type[BaseHTTPRequestHandler]:
37	    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
38	        protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
39	
40	        def log_message(self, format: str, *args: Any) -> None:
41	            return
42	
43	        def _json(self, status: int, value: Any) -> None:
44	            body = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
45	            self.send_response(status)
46	            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
47	            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
48	            self.end_headers()
49	            self.wfile.write(body)
50	
51	        def _body(self) -> Any:
52	            content_type = self.headers.get("Content-Type", "")
53	            if content_type.split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower() != "application/json":
54	                raise ValidationError("Content-Type must be application/json")
55	            try:
56	                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
57	                if length < 0 or length > 1_000_000:
58	                    raise ValueError
59	                return json.loads(self.rfile.read(length))
60	            except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
61	                raise ValidationError("request body must be valid JSON") from error
62	
63	        def _segments(self) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, list[str]]]:
64	            split = urlsplit(self.path)
65	            parts = [unquote(part) for part in split.path.split("/") if part]
66	            return parts, parse_qs(split.query, keep_blank_values=True)
67	
68	        def _instant_parameter(self, query: dict[str, list[str]], name: str) -> int | None:
69	            raw = one(query, name)
70	            return None if raw is None else instant(raw, name)
71	
72	        def _dispatch(self) -> tuple[int, Any]:
73	            parts, query = self._segments()
74	            key = self.headers.get("Idempotency-Key")
75	            if parts == ["health"] and self.command == "GET":
76	                only(query, set())
77	                return 200, {"status": "ok"}
78	            if parts == ["batch"]:
79	                if self.command != "POST":

83	            if parts == ["diff"]:

85	            if parts and parts[0] == "entities":

90	            self, parts: list[str], query: dict[str, list[str]], key: str | None
91	        ) -> tuple[int, Any]:
92	            if len(parts) == 1:
93	                if self.command != "POST":
94	                    raise NotFoundError("route was not found")
95	                only(query, set())
96	                return 201, service.create_entity(parts[0], self._body(), key)
97	            if len(parts) == 2:
98	                entity_type, entity_id = parts
99	                if self.command == "PUT":
100	                    only(query, set())
101	                    return 200, service.apply_correction(entity_type, entity_id, self._body(), key)
102	                if self.command == "GET":
103	                    only(query, {"as_of", "known_at"})
104	                    return 200, service.entity_as_of(
105	                        entity_type,
106	                        entity_id,
107	                        self._instant_parameter(query, "as_of"),
108	                        self._instant_parameter(query, "known_at"),
109	                    )
110	                raise NotFoundError("route was not found")
111	            if len(parts) == 3 and parts[2] == "history" and self.command == "GET":
112	                only(query, {"known_at"})
113	                return 200, service.history(
114	                    parts[0], parts[1], self._instant_parameter(query, "known_at")
115	                )
116	            raise NotFoundError("route was not found")
117	
118	        def _diff(self, query: dict[str, list[str]]) -> tuple[int, Any]:
119	            if self.command != "GET":
120	                raise NotFoundError("route was not found")
121	            only(query, {"type", "id", "from", "to", "known_at", "attribute"})
122	            entity_type = one(query, "type")
123	            entity_id = one(query, "id")

129	                raise ValidationError("diff requires both from and to")

133	            return 200, service.diff(

135	                entity_id,

137	                instant(raw_to, "to"),
138	                self._instant_parameter(query, "known_at"),
139	                names,

142	        def _handle(self) -> None:
143	            try:
144	                status, response = self._dispatch()
145	                self._json(status, response)
146	            except TimeVaultError as error:
147	                self._json(error.status, {"error": {"code": error.code, "message": str(error)}})
148	            except Exception:
149	                self._json(500, {"error": {"code": "internal_error", "message": "internal server error"}})
150	
151	        do_GET = _handle
152	        do_POST = _handle
153	        do_PUT = _handle
154	
155	    return Handler

161	    parser.add_argument("--port", default=8080, type=int)
